correctness.rationale: For each stable h the symplectic Euler matrix is elliptic with no real eigenline and preserves its unique positive quadratic metric P_h up to scale. The covariance map and its adjoint have positive-definite Perron eigenmatrices by cone PF and rank-one exclusion. Determinant-root concavity shows spectral radius at least one; equality forces a common P_h, impossible for nonpoint timestep law, proving rho>1. Positive-definite dual eigenmatrix then proves exact weighted expectation rho^k and uniform Euclidean two-sided bounds for every nonzero input and iteration. Exact rational matrix, characteristic polynomial, first-moment decay, finite-step enumeration and jitter perturbation identities were replayed at the actual packaged verifier path. Analytic simple-eigenvalue perturbation establishes the small-jitter coefficient; finite histories alone are not the proof.

value.rationale: A natural geometric-probabilistic numerical method preserves symplecticity and each individual step lies strictly inside the deterministic stability interval, yet any nonzero iid timestep variability yields uniformly exponential expected-energy inflation at infinite step horizon. This resolves an all-time reliability question outside the source finite-horizon theorem, with an exact rational witness where mean decay masks mean-square growth and a sharp quadratic jitter response. It is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary narrow numerical parameter slice. Practical physical-time and nonlinear implications are explicitly unproved.
